chapters.title: The New Game: How Digital Products Really Make Money
chapters.subtitle: The honest maths behind 'sales every minute', and the machine you will build to get there
chapters.mentor_intro: You told me what you want: sales every minute, notifications that never stop, and people looking at your results and asking, 'who is this guy?' I like that. Big ambition is fuel. But fuel without a map just burns. So in this first chapter I give you the map. We start with the honest maths: what one sale per minute really means, and the ladder that takes you there one step at a time. Then I teach you the numbers every product seller must know from day one: price, fees, order bumps, upsells, average order value, cost per purchase, and the big difference between revenue, profit and cash. You already have ten products in three families. That is a huge head start. Now you need to see how they make money together, as one system. By the end of this chapter you will have your own money map and a simple daily dashboard. You stop guessing. You start measuring. Let's go.
learning_goals: Calculate what 'one sale per minute' really means and set honest, step-by-step targets.
Explain price, platform fees, order bump, upsell, downsell, bundle and average order value in simple words.
Separate revenue, profit and cash so big numbers never fool you.
Map your 3 product families onto the product ladder and the full sales machine.
Build a daily dashboard sheet that tracks visits, sales, AOV, revenue and ad spend.

sections.heading: The dream, and the honest maths

blocks.text: Let's put your dream into numbers. One sale per minute is 60 sales per hour. That is **1,440 sales per day**. At R$27 each, that is about R$39.000 per day, around USD 7,000. (In this book, reais are written the Brazilian way: a dot for thousands and a comma for cents, like R$1.200,50. You will use this format on your sales pages.) Products at that level exist. But they are top products, usually pushed by big ad budgets or by armies of affiliates (afiliados: people who sell your product for a commission). Nobody starts there. Everyone who gets there climbs a ladder, one step at a time.

blocks.title: About 'a million in 15 days'
blocks.text: You will see screenshots like that. Be careful. These numbers are usually **gross revenue** (faturamento bruto), before ad spend and refunds. Very often the story itself is marketing to sell a course. You never see their costs. Do not compare your day 3 with someone else's best edited day.

I will not promise you income. Nobody honest can. What I promise is a way to see, every single day, whether you are climbing. Each step of the ladder is about ten times bigger than the one before. And each step teaches you exactly what the next one needs.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Open your notes and write three lines: 'My first sale by: ___', 'My first 10-sale day by: ___', 'My first 100-sale day by: ___'. Pick dates that scare you a little, not dates that are fantasy.

**Unit economics** (economia por unidade) means: how much money you keep from one sale. It starts with three ideas. **Price** (preço) is what the buyer pays. **Platform fee** (taxa da plataforma) is what the checkout company takes for processing the payment and delivering the product. **Net per sale** (líquido por venda) is what is left for you. Most platforms charge a percentage plus a **fixed fee** (taxa fixa) on every sale. That fixed part is the silent killer of cheap products.

blocks.title: The R$2,49 lesson
blocks.text: Hotmart's Brazil fee is 9.9% + R$2,49 per sale (the R$2,49 fixed fee applies since 21 Sep 2026). On a R$27 product: 9.9% is R$2,67, plus R$2,49 = R$5,16. That is about 19% of the price. Now imagine selling the R$9,90 Desafio das 52 Semanas: Kit Poupança alone: 9.9% is R$0,98, plus R$2,49 = R$3,47. That is about 35% of the price, gone. This is why we sell a R$27 front product and put the small products next to it as bumps, instead of selling them alone.

blocks.title: One R$27 sale, three fee scenarios
These fees are not final for you
blocks.text: EscalePay's fee appears in two versions: 10%, or 8% + USD 0.50. The company also says it sells in 190 countries and pays out to M-Pesa, e-Mola or bank in MZN. None of the international selling has been independently verified: currencies, exchange spread, payout timing, holds and chargebacks (estornos: when a buyer's bank takes the money back) are unknown. Hotmart's fee for a producer living outside Brazil may also look different, so check the fee your account shows at signup. Plan with both EscalePay scenarios, keep Hotmart as backup, and let your own test purchase show the real number. The USD 0.50 in the table uses about R$5,55 per USD, the rate implied by our research. Check today's rate.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Copy the table above into a Google Sheet with formulas. Change only the price cell: first to R$9,90, then to R$47. Watch how the fixed fee changes your share. Ten minutes, and you will never forget this lesson.

sections.heading: The product ladder: front, bump, upsell, downsell, bundle

blocks.title: The five steps of the ladder
items: **Front product** (produto principal): the main offer people see in your content. Low price, easy yes. All of yours are R$27.
**Order bump** (oferta no checkout): a small extra the buyer adds with one click on the payment page, before paying.
**Upsell** (oferta pós-compra): a bigger offer shown right after the purchase, often bought with one click.
**Downsell** (oferta alternativa mais barata): a lighter or cheaper option shown only to people who said no to the upsell.
**Bundle** (pacote ou combo): many products together for one price.

blocks.text: The bundle sits on top of everything: **'Mega Kit 2027: Tudo em Um'**, with all 9 products. The honest anchor (preço âncora: the 'normal' price you compare against) is R$207,60, the sum of the separate prices. It sells for R$67 on Black Friday (27-30 Nov 2026), then R$97. Honest anchor means real numbers: recalculate the sum from your final prices before you publish.

blocks.title: Average order value, step by step (example numbers)
blocks.text: **Average order value** (ticket médio, or AOV) = total revenue ÷ number of orders. Imagine 100 people buy the Caderno do Casal: 100 × R$27 = R$2.700. Say 30% also add the R$12,90 bump: 30 × R$12,90 = R$387. Say 8% take the R$27 upsell: 8 × R$27 = R$216. Total: R$3.303 ÷ 100 orders = **about R$33 per order** before fees. Same visitors, same content, about 22% more money per buyer. The 30% and 8% are example rates, not promises. Your real rates will come from your dashboard.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: For each family, complete one sentence: 'The bump helps the buyer ___ right now. The upsell gives the bigger result of ___.' If you cannot fill the blanks, that step of the ladder is weak.

sections.heading: Revenue, profit, cash and cost per purchase

blocks.title: Five words that protect you
items: **Revenue** (faturamento): all the money buyers paid. The big number in screenshots.
**Profit** (lucro): revenue minus platform fees, refunds, ad spend, taxes and tools. The number that pays your life.
**Cash** (dinheiro em caixa): money already in your M-Pesa, e-Mola or bank. Money waiting in a platform balance is not cash yet.
**Cost per purchase** (custo por compra, or CPA): ad spend ÷ number of purchases from those ads.
**Conversion rate** (taxa de conversão): the share of visitors who buy. 2 buyers from 100 visitors = 2%.

blocks.title: One ad day (example numbers)
blocks.text: You spend R$25 on Meta ads. Since 1 Jan 2026, Meta adds about 12.15% in Brazilian taxes, so the real cost is about R$28. You get 1 purchase with an order of R$33. After a 10% fee you keep R$29,70. Profit: about R$1,70. Your cost per purchase (R$28) is below your order value (R$33), so the rule says you may continue. But look how thin it is, and refunds are not even counted yet. That rule is a limit, not a goal.

blocks.title: Cash is king, and cash can get stuck
blocks.text: Rules for every platform: withdraw often, time how long each payout takes, never keep a big balance. Hotmart pays foreign producers through Payoneer in USD; third-party sources mention about 2% to withdraw and up to 2.75% for conversion, so check this at signup. In Mozambique, Banco de Moçambique Aviso 1/GBM/2025 required converting 50% of export earnings; it was temporary and may end around Oct 2026, so check the current rule. Taxes too: 16% VAT (IVA) on digital goods and services is reported, and the ISPC simplified tax may apply. Check with the AT (Autoridade Tributária, the tax authority) or an accountant before the money gets big.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Write your profit formula at the top of your sheet: Profit = Revenue - fees - refunds - ad spend (with tax) - tools. Repeat it in your head every time someone shows you a revenue screenshot.

sections.heading: The whole machine and your launch calendar

blocks.title: The machine, in order
items: **Product**: the PDF, planner or spreadsheet. Your 10 products are built.
**Page** (página de vendas): your sales page, built in Lovable on your own domain.
**Checkout** (página de pagamento): EscalePay, with Hotmart as backup and second channel. Bumps and upsells live here.
**Traffic** (tráfego): faceless short videos, Pinterest pins, WhatsApp and Telegram channels.
**Affiliates**: people who sell for a 50% commission on your front products.
**Ads** (anúncios pagos): only after organic sales. Small tests of R$20-30/day per product for 5-7 days.
**Repeat**: read the dashboard, fix the weakest step, launch the next product.

blocks.title: Your launch calendar
rows: Teachers buy Nov to early Dec
The honest price after the promo

blocks.text: Notice the order. You do not launch three things at once. You launch one, learn for a few days, then copy what worked into the next. November is Hotmart's strongest month and January the second strongest, so the calendar follows the buyers. Every family comes with a launch kit: sales copy, Lovable prompts, Gemini image prompts, a 30-day faceless content calendar, an affiliate kit, an ads plan and a 72-hour plan. The kits save time. Your attention is still the scarce resource.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Choose your Day 1 as a real date. Put Day 1, Day 5, Day 8 and 27 Nov in your calendar with reminders.

sections.heading: Mindset: speed with quality, and the ethics wall

blocks.text: Speed is your advantage. Claude drafts, Gemini makes images, Lovable builds pages. You can do in days what took others months. But speed without quality creates refunds, angry comments and affiliates who never come back. In Brazil the buyer has 7 days to cancel an online purchase (CDC art. 49, the Consumer Code), and you will honour it every time. So the goal is not 'fast'. The goal is fast **and** good enough that people keep it.

blocks.title: The ethics wall: we never cross it
items: No fake testimonials, fake numbers, fake rankings or fake before/after.
No fake scarcity: no countdown that resets, no 'last 3 copies' of a PDF.
No income, health or result guarantees.
Honest anchors only: a 'from' price must be real.
Label AI where platforms require it (TikTok requires labels on realistic AI people and scenes).
Never spam people on WhatsApp, Telegram or in comments.

blocks.text: Fast is a weapon. Fake is a trap. Build the kind of name affiliates are proud to sell.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Copy the ethics wall into the first tab of your dashboard sheet. Before you publish any page, video or ad, read it once.

key_takeaways: One sale per minute is 1,440 sales per day: top-product level. You reach it by climbing first sale, then 10/day, then 100/day.
Fixed per-sale fees (like Hotmart's R$2,49) eat cheap products, so sell a R$27 front and offer small products as bumps.
Bumps and upsells raise average order value without more visitors: R$27 becomes about R$33 in our example.
Revenue is not profit, and profit is not cash: withdraw often and never keep big balances.
Run ads only after organic sales, and only while cost per purchase stays below average order value.
Speed with quality, behind the ethics wall: no fake proof, no guarantees, honour every refund.

challenge.title: Your money map
challenge.mission: Turn Family 1 into numbers you understand: AOV, profit per 100 visitors under two fee scenarios, 10-day targets, and a daily dashboard you will use from Day 1.
steps: Create a Google Sheet called 'Money Map' with a tab 'Family 1'. Enter the prices: front R$27, bump R$12,90, upsell R$27, downsell R$17.
Enter example take rates (bump 30%, upsell 8%) and calculate AOV with formulas. Check: you should get about R$33.
Enter an example conversion rate of 2% (fictional): 100 visitors = 2 orders. Calculate revenue for 100 visitors, treating each order as one transaction for now.
Calculate what you keep under Scenario A (10%) and Scenario B (8% + USD 0.50 per order, at today's exchange rate). With about R$5,55 per USD you should land near R$59 for A and R$55 for B.
Change the price cell until Scenario B keeps more than Scenario A. Write that price (near R$139 at R$5,55 per USD) and one sentence on why the fixed fee hurts cheap products.
Write your 10-day targets for visits, sales and AOV. Keep them honest, not fantasy.
Add a tab 'Dashboard' with columns Date, Visits, Sales, AOV, Revenue, Ad spend (AOV = Revenue ÷ Sales). Fill in today's row, even if it is all zeros.
challenge.proof: A screenshot of your Money Map showing both fee scenarios, the break-even price, your 10-day targets and the Dashboard tab with today's row.
challenge.bonus: Add a third scenario for Hotmart Brazil (9.9% + R$2,49) and a cell that shows how many visitors you need for one sale at your example conversion rate.

quiz.question: How many sales per day is 'one sale per minute'?
quiz.explanation: 60 sales per hour × 24 hours = 1,440 sales per day. That is top-product territory, reached by climbing the ladder.

quiz.question: Why is a R$9,90 product weak when sold alone on a platform with a R$2,49 fixed fee?
options: Brazilians never buy cheap products
The fixed fee takes a much bigger share of a small price
Pix does not accept prices under R$10
Affiliates are not allowed to sell it
quiz.explanation: On Hotmart, R$2,49 plus 9.9% eats about 35% of R$9,90. As a bump on a R$27 order, the small product adds value without that problem.

quiz.question: Which of these is profit?
options: The total sales number in a screenshot
Revenue minus fees, refunds, ad spend, taxes and tools
The balance waiting in your platform account
The price of your front product
quiz.explanation: Revenue is what buyers paid; profit is what remains after all costs. Cash is what actually reaches your M-Pesa, e-Mola or bank.

glossary.meaning: Total revenue divided by the number of orders: how much one buyer spends on average.
A small extra product the buyer adds with one click on the payment page.
A bigger offer shown right after the purchase.
Ad spend divided by the number of purchases those ads brought.
The share of visitors who buy, for example 2 buyers from 100 visitors = 2%.
What is left after fees, refunds, ads, taxes and tools.

chapters.title: The Lusophone Market Playbook
chapters.subtitle: Brazil first, the rest of the Portuguese-speaking world next, and how to read the market yourself
chapters.mentor_intro: Portuguese is spoken on several continents, so it looks like one giant market. It is not. It is several markets, with different money, different payment apps, different buying power and even different ways to write the same sentence. If you try to sell to all of them on day one, you will sell to none of them well. So we choose. Brazil first. Brazil has the buyers, the instant payments, the platforms and a huge affiliate culture. Later comes one PT-PT edition for Portugal, Angola and Mozambique. There is a twist in your story. You write European/Mozambican Portuguese naturally. That is a gift, because you understand language deeply. It is also a trap, because one 'ficheiro' on a Brazilian page says 'foreigner' louder than any accent. In this chapter you learn what sells and when, how to sound Brazilian, which trust signals close the sale, and a 30-minute weekly routine to find and test new ideas yourself. Let's go scouting.
learning_goals: Explain why Brazil is your first market and what Brazilian buyers expect on price and payment.
Plan your year around Brazil's buying seasons: Black Friday, Christmas with the 13th salary, and January.
Write and check PT-BR copy that sounds Brazilian, not Portuguese or Mozambican.
Add the trust signals that make a Brazilian buyer comfortable paying a foreign seller.
Run a 30-minute weekly trend routine and score ideas before you build them.

blocks.text: Three reasons. **Size**: WhatsApp alone has more than 120 million users in Brazil. **Payments**: Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) was 42% of Brazilian e-commerce value in 2025, with cards at 40%. A buyer can pay R$27 in seconds from the phone. **Affiliate culture**: Brazil has a big community of people who sell other people's products for a commission. On Hotmart, commissions run from 30% to 80%; on Kiwify, from 40% to 70%. You offer 50% on front products, inside the 40-60% range recommended for low-ticket products.

blocks.title: Price norms in Brazil
items: **Low-ticket** (produto de ticket baixo: a cheap product) digital products usually sit between R$19,90 and R$47.
Fixed per-sale fees make very cheap products painful, so R$27 + bumps is the sweet spot.
Your catalog uses both price styles buyers know: round (R$27, R$37) and ',90' (R$12,90, R$9,90).
**Interest-free instalments** (parcelamento sem juros) matter to Brazilian buyers, especially on bigger prices like the R$97 Mega Kit. Check if your checkout offers them.

blocks.text: You are a foreign seller in Brazil. That is fine. But you must earn trust twice: once with the product, and once with the feeling that 'this seller is serious and reachable'. Everything in this chapter serves both.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Search 'planner financeiro' on the Hotmart marketplace and write down 5 prices you see. Compare them with your R$27. You are now thinking like a Brazilian buyer.

blocks.title: Top categories in Brazil in 2026 (and where you stand)
items: Make-money-online: the biggest, but saturated and risky to advertise. We skip it.
AI
TikTok Shop
Beauty and relationships (low ticket): your Caderno do Casal lives here.
Faith and devotionals: your Devocional do Casal and Natal na EBD (Escola Bíblica Dominical, Sunday Bible school).
Recipes
Kids and teacher printables: your Kit Natal na Escola.
Crafts

blocks.title: Brazil's buying calendar
rows: Gifts and extra money; teachers buy Nov-early Dec
Kit Natal; Caderno do Casal as a gift

blocks.text: The **13th salary** (13º salário) is an extra month of pay that Brazilian workers with formal jobs receive near the end of the year. More money in pockets plus the gift season is why November and December matter so much. In January 2026, Hotmart transactions were 24% above the average of the other months: people start the year wanting to organise their lives and money. Check the exact 13th salary payment dates each year before you plan promotions around them.

blocks.title: Why our 3 families, and what we said no to
Popular is not the same as right for you
blocks.text: Make-money-online is a top category, and we still said no. Meta bans get-rich-quick promises, and CONAR (Brazil's advertising self-regulation council) acts against misleading ads. A category you cannot advertise safely is a category that can get your accounts blocked. Choose products you can promote with a calm heart.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Add three dates to your calendar: 27 Nov (Black Friday), 1 Dec ('Christmas kit last push'), and 26 Dec ('January planner push starts'). The last two are my suggested working dates, not official ones.

Brazilian sales copy has three marks. **Você** and its verb forms, never tu forms like 'vais', 'abre' or 'estás'. **Gerúndio** (the -ndo form: 'estou organizando', not 'estou a organizar'). And **Brazilian vocabulary**: celular, planilha, arquivo, baixar, tela. Brazilians also often drop the article before 'meu/seu' ('minhas finanças', not 'as minhas finanças'). Brazilian buyers notice the difference in one line. Portuguese buyers notice it too, the other way round: Portugal generally dislikes PT-BR. That is why we will make a separate PT-PT edition later.

blocks.title: Same idea, two Portugueses (formal business tone)
rows: You will download the file now
Você vai baixar o arquivo agora
Estou a organizar as minhas finanças

blocks.text: One PT-PT word on a Brazilian page ('ficheiro', 'telemóvel', 'estás a', 'descarregar') makes the buyer feel the seller is far away. Far away feels risky. Risky means no Pix.

blocks.title: Do it now: your PT-BR swap list
items: Create a doc called 'PT-BR swap list' with two columns: 'I naturally write' and 'Brazil writes'.
Add the 6 pairs from the table above.
Ask Claude for 20 more pairs common on sales pages and product files, then check each one yourself.
Search every text (Ctrl+F) for each word in the left column before you publish it.

blocks.title: The trust checklist
items: **Pix and card at checkout**, with prices in reais (R$27), never only in USD.
**A clear guarantee**: Brazil's Consumer Code (CDC art. 49) gives 7 days to cancel an online purchase. Show it clearly and honour it.

**Seller identification**: Decreto 7.962/2013 asks online sellers to show name, identification and contact. Check how a foreign seller should show this (your NUIT, the Mozambican tax number? the platform's data?) before launch.
**Support in Portuguese**: an email or WhatsApp that answers in PT-BR.
**Privacy policy** (política de privacidade) in Portuguese under LGPD, Brazil's data protection law, plus consent before you send marketing messages.
**Real previews**: a flip-through video and sample pages. Never fake reviews.

blocks.title: Trust block for your sales page (PT-BR)
blocks.text: Pagamento via Pix ou cartão. Você recebe o acesso logo após a confirmação do pagamento. Garantia de 7 dias: se o material não for para você, é só pedir o reembolso dentro de 7 dias após a compra. Ficou com alguma dúvida? Fale com a gente pelo e-mail [seu e-mail]. Respondemos em português, de segunda a sexta.

blocks.title: Test before you promote
blocks.text: Make two real test purchases before any promotion: one by Pix from a Brazilian buyer (a friend or contact in Brazil) and one by card. Check that the price shows in R$, Pix works, the product arrives, the refund works, and how long the payout takes. EscalePay's international selling is not independently verified, so this test is not optional.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Open your Lovable sales page for Caderno do Casal and tick each item on the trust checklist. Every missing item goes on today's to-do list. Adjust the script to match how your platform really delivers access, and only promise support hours you can really keep.

sections.heading: Portugal, Angola, Mozambique: the next editions

blocks.title: The other markets, honestly
rows: Foreign currency and cards very restricted
Hard to get paid for now

blocks.text: The plan: after Brazil proves the products, create **one PT-PT edition** for Portugal, Angola and Mozambique together. Same products, rewritten in European Portuguese (a fazer, ficheiro, telemóvel), with local examples and local prices. English and Spanish editions come after that.

blocks.title: Europe has its own rules
blocks.text: In the EU and Portugal, buyers have 14 days to withdraw unless they tick an express consent checkbox to get the download immediately. And EU VAT (IVA) applies from the first B2C e-book sale (a sale to a private person, not a company) for non-EU sellers, unless the platform is the merchant of record (the company that legally sells and handles the tax). Do not price in EUR until you check this with your platform.

I know Mozambique is home, and it is tempting to sell first to people you know. Do it later, with joy, with local prices and local payments. For now, home is your base and Brazil is your market. Today, just write 'PT-PT edition: after Brazil proof' in your plan and move on.

sections.heading: Your 30-minute trend routine and idea validation

blocks.title: The weekly routine (set a 30-minute timer)
items: Minutes 0-6, **Hotmart marketplace**: browse your categories. Note products that appear again and again, their prices and their promises.

Minutes 6-12, **TikTok search**: type your niche in Portuguese ('planner financeiro', 'atividades de natal', 'perguntas para casais'). Note the autocomplete suggestions and videos with comments asking 'onde compra?'.
Minutes 12-18, **Pinterest Trends**: look for rising searches about planners and printables. If Brazil data is not available, use the suggestions in Pinterest search.
Minutes 18-24, **Google Trends**: set Brazil, last 12 months. Compare 2-3 terms and see the season curve.

Minutes 24-30, **Kiwify/Cakto top lists**: see what sells now, if you can access them. (Selling on Kiwify needs a Brazilian CPF and bank account, so for you it is a research tool.) Log every idea with one link or screenshot as evidence.

blocks.title: Validate before you build: 4 questions
items: **Search volume** (volume de busca): do people search for it? Check the Google Trends curve, TikTok and Pinterest suggestions.
**Competitors** (concorrentes): are others selling it? Some competition is good, because it proves there is money. Zero competitors can mean zero buyers.
**Price**: can it sell in the R$19,90-47 range and carry a bump?
**Angle** (ângulo): what makes yours different? A specific audience, a specific moment, a better format.

blocks.text: Then score each idea from 1 (bad) to 5 (great) on five criteria: **D** = demand, **G** = competition gap (room for you), **E** = ease to build, **C** = compliance (legal and platform safety), **M** = margin (money left after fees). The maximum total is 25.

blocks.title: Validating one idea (fictional evidence)
blocks.text: You search 'atividades de páscoa' on TikTok and see teacher videos with comments asking for the file. Google Trends for Brazil shows the term rising before Easter. On Hotmart you find several kits at different prices. Your angle: 'pronto para imprimir em preto e branco, para turmas de 4 a 6 anos'. It is secular, easy to build from your Christmas kit template, and fits R$27 + a bump. Score 20: shortlist it and schedule it well before the season.

blocks.title: Compliance is a gate, not a score
blocks.text: Any idea with compliance 1 is out, no matter how high the total is. Diet plans (reserved for nutritionists in Brazil), copied characters, guaranteed earnings: no. Now go run the routine in the challenge.

key_takeaways: Brazil first: a huge audience, Pix (42% of e-commerce value in 2025) and a strong affiliate culture.
Plan your year around Black Friday (27 Nov 2026), Christmas with the 13th salary, and January.
Write in PT-BR (você, gerúndio, Brazilian words); one PT-PT word can cost you the sale.
Trust sells: R$ prices, Pix, a 7-day guarantee, clear seller identification, Portuguese support and an LGPD privacy policy.
Portugal, Angola and Mozambique come later with one PT-PT edition, after you check payments and EU VAT.
Validate before you build: search volume, competitors, price and angle. Compliance is a gate.

challenge.title: Market scout
challenge.mission: Run your first 30-minute trend routine, log 10 product ideas with real evidence, and score them so you know what to build next.
steps: Create a sheet 'Market Scout' with columns: Idea, Evidence (link or screenshot), Prices seen, Demand, Gap, Ease, Compliance, Margin, Total.
Set a 30-minute timer and run the routine: Hotmart marketplace, TikTok search, Pinterest Trends, Google Trends (Brazil), Kiwify/Cakto top lists.
Log 10 ideas, each with at least one piece of evidence.
Score each idea 1-5 on the five criteria. Mark any idea with compliance 1 as 'Out'.
Pick your top 3 and write one angle sentence in PT-BR for each.
Write next to each top idea which season it fits (Black Friday, Christmas, January, other).
challenge.proof: Your Market Scout sheet with 10 scored ideas, evidence links, and the top 3 highlighted with their PT-BR angles.
challenge.bonus: Turn your number 1 idea into a one-line PT-BR promise and check every word against your PT-BR swap list.

quiz.question: Which payment method had the biggest share of Brazilian e-commerce value in 2025?
options: Cards
Pix
PayPal
Bank transfer from abroad
quiz.explanation: Pix was 42% of e-commerce value in 2025, with cards at 40%. That is why Pix at checkout is a must for Brazilian buyers.

quiz.question: Which sentence is PT-BR?
options: Estou a organizar as minhas finanças
Estou organizando minhas finanças
Vai descarregar o ficheiro agora
quiz.explanation: Brazilian Portuguese uses the gerúndio ('organizando'). 'Estou a organizar' and 'descarregar o ficheiro' are European Portuguese.

quiz.question: An idea scores 5 on demand and margin but 1 on compliance. What do you do?
options: Build it fast before others do
Build it but avoid ads
Reject it: compliance is a gate
Sell it only to affiliates
quiz.explanation: Compliance is a gate, not a score. A product you cannot sell safely can block your accounts and hurt your name.

glossary.meaning: Brazil's instant payment system; buyers pay in seconds from their phone.
Paying a price in several parts without extra cost to the buyer.
How demand goes up and down at certain times of the year.
An extra month of pay Brazilian workers with formal jobs receive near the end of the year.
Anything on your page that shows the buyer you are real, reachable and fair.
The company that legally sells the product and handles taxes like VAT.

chapters.title: Your Product Factory
chapters.subtitle: Build premium faceless products fast, safely, and on a two-week rhythm
chapters.mentor_intro: You already have ten products. Most beginners would love that. But here is the truth about this market: products are now easy to make, so easy products are worth almost nothing. Anyone can ask an AI for '50 pages about money' in one minute. Buyers know it. Platforms know it. The products that survive are the ones that feel made by someone who cared. In this chapter I show you how to run a small factory: a repeatable workflow where Claude drafts, you edit and decide, and every file passes a quality check before a buyer sees it. You will learn the PT-BR localisation checklist, printable design rules, spreadsheets that really work in Google Sheets, compliance by niche and the copyright traps that hurt faceless sellers. Then we design the ladder properly: what makes a great bump and a great upsell. Finally, a rhythm: a new product every two weeks. Quality is not the opposite of speed. Quality is what makes speed worth it.
learning_goals: Apply a premium quality bar so your products earn happy buyers, not refunds.
Run the factory workflow from outline to versioned PDF with Claude, Canva and code-generated layouts.
Check every product for PT-BR language, print quality, spreadsheet function, compliance and copyright.
Design order bumps and upsells that fit naturally with the front product.
Plan a two-week cycle to ship your next products.

sections.heading: The quality bar: why cheap AI and PLR products fail

blocks.text: **PLR** (direitos de revenda: content you buy with the right to resell) and quick AI e-books flood the market. They fail for simple reasons. Buyers find the same thing free on Pinterest, Google or YouTube. They ask for a refund inside the 7 days the law gives them (CDC art. 49). Platforms like Hotmart and Kiwify have content rules and can review or remove products (read their current rules before each new niche; check this). And affiliates stop promoting a product that brings complaints.

blocks.title: The premium bar: every product must have
items: A specific promise for a specific person: '52 encontros para casais que querem se reconectar', not 'dicas de relacionamento'.
A clear structure: a 'Comece aqui' page, how to use it, logical sections.
Original design with consistent fonts and colours.
Perfect PT-BR, every accent correct.
Pages that work on screen and on paper.
Something hard to find free: done-for-you structure, ready to print, saves the buyer hours.

blocks.text: If a buyer can find it free in ten seconds, it is not a product. It is a future refund.

Never publish text you have not read line by line. Claude drafts fast and well, but it can invent facts, mix PT-PT with PT-BR, or repeat itself. You are the editor, and your brand is the name behind the product.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Open Caderno do Casal and read 5 random pages as a stranger who paid R$27. Write one honest sentence: 'Worth it because ___' or 'Not yet because ___'.

blocks.title: From idea to file
items: **Outline** (estrutura): write the promise, the audience, the sections and the page count. One page.
**Draft with Claude** in PT-BR, one section at a time, following your outline and tone.
**Edit** yourself: cut, fix, add your angle, run the PT-BR swap list and the compliance check.
**Design**: use Canva for covers and unique pages, and code-generated layouts for repeated pages. Gemini makes art without text; you add titles in Canva.
**Test print**: print 3 real pages on A4. Check margins, ink, readability and writing space.
**Export the PDF**: compressed images, correct page order, every link tested.
**Save versions** (controle de versão, version control): name it v1.0, keep a changelog (registro de mudanças), store master files in one Drive folder.

blocks.title: Code-generated layouts
blocks.text: For repeated pages, ask Claude: 'Create an A4 HTML page with print CSS, 1.5 cm margins, a title at the top, 8 writing lines and a page number at the bottom, black and white.' Then generate all 52 encounter pages with different titles and print to PDF from the browser. Every page has the same layout, and one fix takes one minute instead of 52.
With AI, writing is no longer the bottleneck. Your checking is. Protect your editing hours: phone away, one product at a time.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Create one Drive folder per product with 4 subfolders: 01_Texto, 02_Design, 03_Exportados, 04_Marketing. Move your current files into them.

blocks.title: PT-BR localisation checklist
items: Você + gerúndio everywhere.
Brazilian words: celular, planilha, arquivo, baixar, cadastro, tela.
Money as R$27,90 (comma for cents, dot for thousands: R$1.200,00).
Dates as DD/MM/AAAA.
Brazilian examples: Pix, salário, 13º salário, real prices in reais.
All accents correct: ç, ã, õ, é, ê.
Kit Natal: December is summer in Brazil, so choose your Christmas imagery on purpose.

blocks.title: Printable design rules
items: **A4** size for every printable.
Keep important content inside a safe margin (I use at least 1.5 cm): home printers often cut the edges.
**Ink-friendly**: white backgrounds, line art, no full-page dark fills. Keep strong colour for the cover.
Check every page in grayscale (escala de cinza).
Text big enough to read once printed. Test it on paper.
Writing lines spaced for real handwriting, plus page numbers.

blocks.title: Spreadsheets that work in Google Sheets
items: Set File > Settings > Locale to Brasil so R$ and commas display correctly.
In the Brazil locale, formulas use ';' as separator. Test every formula.
Add a 'Comece aqui' tab with simple instructions.
Protect the cells that contain formulas.
Deliver a 'make a copy' link (change /edit to /copy at the end of the link) so each buyer gets their own copy.
Test it in the Google Sheets phone app. Avoid scripts and macros.

blocks.title: AI images and Portuguese text do not mix
blocks.text: Gemini is unreliable when it writes text inside images: it often breaks accents (ç, ã, é). Generate the art without text, then add every title in Canva, where you control each letter.

blocks.title: Do it now
items: Open page 1 of each front product in grayscale preview.
Check that nothing important sits outside the safe margin.
Open the Planilha Financeira, set the locale to Brasil and test 3 formulas.

blocks.title: Compliance by niche
rows: Secular; ads to adults; no kids' data

blocks.title: Copyright rules
items: No famous characters and no copies of another creator's designs. That is why we rejected Bobbie Goods copies.
No images copied from Google or Pinterest.
Gemini images are generated by you, not copied, but check each one for look-alikes of brands, logos or famous characters. Read Gemini's terms on commercial use (check this).
Check that every font and graphic element allows commercial use.
If a video uses realistic AI people or scenes on TikTok, add the AI label.

blocks.title: Disclaimers for the 'Comece aqui' page (PT-BR)
blocks.text: **Planner Financeiro 2027:** Este material tem caráter exclusivamente educativo. Ele não é recomendação de investimento nem consultoria financeira. **Caderno do Casal:** Este caderno é um material de reflexão e conversa para casais. Ele não substitui acompanhamento psicológico ou terapia. **Devocional do Casal:** As referências bíblicas indicam o trecho para você ler na sua própria Bíblia. Os comentários são paráfrases e reflexões nossas.

blocks.title: Two hard lines in Brazil
blocks.text: Diet plans are reserved for nutritionists, so we do not make them. And for kids' products, your ads speak only to adults (teachers, parents), and you never collect children's data.

blocks.title: Do it now
blocks.text: Add the right disclaimer to the 'Comece aqui' page of each front product and each upsell today.

blocks.title: File naming rules
items: Pattern: Product_Variant_vX-Y. Example: CadernoDoCasal_52Encontros_v1-0.pdf
No spaces, accents or special characters in file names: they can break on some phones and systems.
The version number goes in every file name.
Keep a changelog doc: date, version, what changed.
Keep editable masters separate from exported PDFs.

blocks.text: Buyers usually receive access by email, a members area, or both. How exactly EscalePay and Hotmart deliver your file is something you check in your own test purchase. For spreadsheets, deliver a short PDF with the 'make a copy' link and 3 simple steps. Keep PDFs light enough to download on a phone with mobile data: compress images before export, and check each platform's upload size limit.

blocks.title: Thank-you message (PT-BR)
blocks.text: Olá! Obrigado pela sua compra. Seu material já está disponível. Comece pela página 'Comece aqui': ela explica como imprimir e usar. Se tiver qualquer dificuldade para baixar, é só responder a este e-mail que nós ajudamos você. Bom proveito!

blocks.title: Do it now: the delivery test
items: Check the platform's rules on test purchases, then buy your own product once.
Open the delivery email on your phone.
Download the PDF on mobile data and time it.
Open it on your laptop and click every link.
Print one page.
Request a refund, if the platform allows it, to see the full flow.

sections.heading: Designing the ladder and the two-week rhythm

blocks.title: Order bump vs upsell
rows: One click on the checkout page

blocks.text: The **downsell** is a lighter or cheaper option for people who said no to the upsell: the Planilha alone at R$19,90, or the Devocional at R$17. Be crystal clear about what is included at each price. No tricks.

blocks.title: Family 2, step by step
blocks.text: Front: Planner Financeiro 2027 (R$27) helps the buyer plan the year. Bump: Desafio das 52 Semanas: Kit Poupança (R$9,90) gives an instant, small win: start saving this week. Upsell: Planilha Financeira 2027 + Guia Saia das Dívidas (R$37) automates the numbers and tackles a bigger problem. Downsell: just the Planilha (R$19,90). Each step makes sense after the one before. That is a good ladder.

Every new product should do double duty: a new front with its own ladder, or a new bump or upsell for a family that already sells. Reuse templates, layouts and content. Today, write down which family your 4th product would join.

key_takeaways: Cheap AI and PLR products fail: buyers find them free, ask for refunds, and platforms can remove them.
The factory: outline, Claude drafts, you edit, design, test print, PDF export, version control.
Localise for Brazil, design for real printers (A4, safe margins, ink-friendly) and test spreadsheets with the Brasil locale.
Compliance by niche: no therapy claims, finance educational only, kids' products marketed to adults, Bible references + paraphrase.
Bump = small, instant, complementary. Upsell = bigger outcome. Downsell = lighter, honest alternative.
A two-week cycle turns one-off products into a growing catalog.

challenge.title: Factory test
challenge.mission: Put your three front products through the factory quality check, prove they print well, fix real issues, and outline your 4th product.
steps: Open the three front products: Caderno do Casal, Planner Financeiro 2027 and Kit Natal na Escola.
Run the quality checklist on each (premium bar, PT-BR localisation, print rules, compliance wording, copyright, links) and log every issue in a sheet.
Test-print 3 pages, one from each product, on A4 at home or at a print shop. With no printer, check a 100% print preview in grayscale.
Fix at least 5 issues, save the files as v1.1 and write the changes in your changelog.
Rename the files using the naming rule.
Write the outline of your 4th product idea: promise, audience, 8-12 sections, bump idea, upsell idea and compliance note.
challenge.proof: Your issues log with at least 5 items marked fixed, a photo of the 3 printed pages (or preview screenshots), and the one-page outline of product 4.
challenge.bonus: Build one repeated page with a code-generated layout (Claude HTML + print CSS) and compare it with the Canva version. Keep the better one as your template.

quiz.question: Which is the best order bump for Caderno do Casal?
options: A R$97 online course about marriage
100 Cartões de Perguntas para Casais at R$12,90
A free PDF found on Pinterest
A 12-month finance planner
quiz.explanation: A good bump is small, instant and complementary. The question cards fit the couples' journal perfectly at a low price.

quiz.question: You need a cover image with the title 'Coração em Dia'. What do you do?
options: Ask Gemini to write the title inside the image
Generate the art without text in Gemini and add the title in Canva
Copy a cover image from Pinterest
Skip the accents in the title
quiz.explanation: AI image tools often break Portuguese accents. Make the art without text and add the title in Canva, where you control the letters.

quiz.question: How should the Devocional do Casal use the Bible?
options: Copy full NVI verses on every page
Give references and paraphrase, with no verbatim NVI quotes
Avoid any mention of the Bible
Quote any translation found online
quiz.explanation: The NVI is copyrighted. Give the reference so the buyer reads it in their own Bible, and write your own paraphrase and reflection.

glossary.meaning: Content bought with the right to resell; usually generic and widely copied.
A PDF designed to be printed and used on paper.
The empty area near the page edges where printers may cut.
A list of what changed in each version of a file.
A short note that sets limits, for example 'educational only'.
Adapting language, money, dates and examples to one specific market.
